manifest.name: MiniMax-H3
manifest.blurb: A 50-block DiT over ONE packed 1-D sequence holding text, video and audio rows together. Full self-attention, no cross-attention anywhere. Keyframes and references enter as extra video ROWS, not extra channels.
manifest.shape_note: Shapes for 480 × 832, 5 s @ 24 fps: the f16t4d24 VAE gives 30 × 52 latent frames of 24 ch; the (1,2,2) patch makes 15 · 26 = 390 rows per latent frame.

notes.title: Row order is the caller's job, not the model's
notes.text: build_packed_sequence lays the rows out as text ‖ conditioning ‖ audio ‖ video and returns the tags, the (t,h,w) grid and the index lists. The DiT validates shapes and otherwise trusts that layout completely — which is why a wrong row order fails silently rather than loudly.

notes.title: Padding rows get their own attention document
notes.text: Rows tagged −1 must not exchange attention with live rows. A boolean mask pairing pad-with-pad and live-with-live reproduces the reference's cu_seqlens split. A padless sequence keeps the mask at None so the flash-attention fast path stays available — so dropping padding is faster, not just tidier.

notes.title: Two tasks, two layouts, one mechanism
notes.text: FL2VA packs [text ‖ keyframe rows ‖ target audio ‖ target video] and pins each keyframe to "first" or "last". Ref2VA packs [text ‖ reference blocks ‖ target audio ‖ target video] and lets each reference push the shared clock forward. Different builders, identical idea: extra low-noise video rows at a chosen place on the clock.

notes.title: A reference's text rows are tagged VIDEO, not text
notes.text: Ref2VA writes a short vision block into the prompt presentation for each reference; those prompt rows carry tag 0 (video) rather than 1 (text), so they pick the video row of the AdaLN table. A small detail that matters if you ever rebuild the tags by hand.

notes.title: Why this is noise-augmented and not clean
notes.text: Conditioning rows are mixed to t = 0.999 rather than inserted clean. A clean row sitting next to rows at high noise is far off the distribution the model trained on; augmenting it keeps the whole sequence at a consistent noise scale.

notes.title: Sequence parallelism splits rows, not heads
notes.text: With more than one GPU the sequence is padded to a multiple of the world size and each rank keeps a slice of ROWS; the attention processor all-gathers keys and values. A padded (masked) sequence is rejected outright in this mode.

notes.title: Three differences from Wan's block, and they all matter
notes.text: 1 — no cross-attention sublayer; text is in the sequence instead. 2 — RMSNorm, not LayerNorm. 3 — SwiGLU, not GELU MLP. Plus the taps are selected per row by adaln_indices rather than broadcast to every token.

notes.title: Why there is no cross-attention to add
notes.text: Text rows are in the sequence, so a video row attends to text in exactly this operation. Wan needs a second sublayer (cross_attn) because its text never enters the sequence. One design pays for it in sequence length, the other in parameters and a second attention per block.

expect.first: A Transformer model for joint video + audio generation, introduced in MiniMax-H3.

notes.title: The cost
notes.text: Attention is S × S where S counts text + conditioning + audio + video rows together. Audio is cheap (a handful of rows per latent) but it is still inside the quadratic term, and so is every text token.
